result.title: EASTAR: Event-Anchored Semantic and Task-Adaptive Region Representation Learning
result.comment: 13 pages. Accepted to the 43rd IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering (ICDE 2027)
result.summary: Urban region representation learning supports a wide range of urban analytics tasks by encoding regional functions and interactions, with human mobility serving as a central signal because it directly captures inter-region interactions. However, most mobility-based methods learn from aggregated origin-destination matrices, where trips driven by different activity purposes are mixed into purpose-agnostic interaction patterns. Although static urban attributes such as POIs and land use can enrich region-level semantics, they do not explicitly ground mobility interactions in activity-purpose signals. As a result, downstream adaptation is often performed over entangled embeddings, making it difficult to select task-relevant functional semantics. To address these limitations, we propose EASTAR, an event-anchored and task-adaptive framework for urban region representation learning. EASTAR treats offline activity events as sparse semantic anchors and uses them to factorize aggregated mobility representations into multiple purpose-related semantic channels. It further introduces free channels to capture latent mobility patterns not covered by event data and a global channel to preserve overall spatial structure. To adapt the learned channel space to different downstream objectives, EASTAR designs a task-adaptive prompt router that initializes task-channel relevance from LLM-derived priors and refines the routing weights through downstream supervision. Experiments on two real-world urban datasets across four prediction tasks show that EASTAR consistently outperforms representative baselines, achieving up to 39.15% reduction in MAE. Ablation and interpretability analyses further demonstrate the effectiveness of event anchoring, semantic channel construction, and task-adaptive routing.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 EASTAR，用线下活动事件作为稀疏语义锚点，把聚合移动性表示分解为多个活动目的相关的语义通道，并加入自由通道与全局通道，再用任务自适应路由权重适配下游城市预测任务。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是城市区域嵌入与移动性、POI 等空间统计建模，不涉及视觉或多模态推理状态，也没有证据获取、停止决策或视觉信息保留的内容；「语义通道分解」与「路由」仅为通用表示分解手段，无可核查的 LVR 借鉴线索。
